title: Temurah 9
description: Substitution across kinds, sexes and blemishes, the two instances of “good” in the verse, exchanging for another’s animal, Rabbi Shimon’s one-for-one rule and whether one may substitute again, and Rabbi Avin’s unresolved dilemmas about a guilt offering that changed body or sanctity.
topics: 🐑 Flock for herd, sheep for goats, males for females, unblemished for blemished
⚖️ “Good for bad”: only an animal consecrated before its blemish effects substitution
🔁 Abaye and Rava on the two instances of “good”, and punishing from an a fortiori inference
🤝 “He shall not exchange it”: substituting for another person’s consecrated animal
💯 One for a hundred and a hundred for one, or only one for one? Rabbi Shimon’s verses
🔂 Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yoḥanan: may one substitute and then substitute again?
❓ Rabbi Avin’s guilt offering: two bodies, two sanctities, and teiku
➕ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: a second consecration adds no fifth

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ מְמִירִין מִן הַצֹּאן עַל הַבָּקָר, וּמִן הַבָּקָר עַל הַצֹּאן, וּמִן הַכְּבָשִׂים עַל הָעִזִּים, וּמִן הָעִזִּים עַל הַכְּבָשִׂים, מִן הַזְּכָרִים עַל הַנְּקֵבוֹת, וּמִן הַנְּקֵבוֹת עַל הַזְּכָרִים, מִן הַתְּמִימִים עַל בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין, מִן בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין עַל הַתְּמִימִים.

a3.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ רַע בְּטוֹב״, וְאֵיזֶהוּ ״טוֹב בְּרָע״? בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן.

a4.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה״ — מִכָּאן שֶׁמְּמִירִין מִן הַצֹּאן עַל הַבָּקָר, וּמִן הַבָּקָר עַל הַצֹּאן, מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים עַל הָעִזִּים, וּמִן הָעִזִּים עַל הַכְּבָשִׂים, וּמִן הַזְּכָרִים עַל הַנְּקֵבוֹת, וּמִן הַנְּקֵבוֹת עַל הַזְּכָרִים, וּמִן בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין עַל הַתְּמִימִים, וּמִן הַתְּמִימִים עַל בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין.

a5.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ קָדַם מוּם לְהֶקְדֵּישָׁן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ רַע בְּטוֹב״, וְאֵיזֶהוּ ״טוֹב בְּרָע״? בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן.

a6.he: מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נֵימָא קְרָא ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ רַע בּוֹ״, ״בְּטוֹב״ אַחְרִינָא לְמָה לִי? שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: טוֹב מֵעִיקָּרוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, רַע מֵעִיקָּרוֹ אֵין עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

a7.he: רָבָא אָמַר: תַּרְוַויְיהוּ ״טוֹב״ יַיתּוֹרֵי מְיַיתְּרִי. אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ בְּרָע אוֹ רַע בּוֹ״, לְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב תַּרְוַיְיהוּ ״טוֹב״? חַד ״טוֹב״ — אֲפִילּוּ בְּטוֹב נָמֵי, כִּי מֵמִיר לָקֵי. וְאִידַּךְ ״טוֹב״ — מֵעִיקָּרוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, רַע מֵעִיקָּרוֹ אֵין עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

a8.he: וְאַבָּיֵי אָמַר: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא, וּמָה טוֹב בְּרָע, דְּעַלּוֹיֵי קָא מְעַלֵּי לֵיהּ — לָקֵי, טוֹב בְּטוֹב, דְּכִי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּלָקֵי!

a9.he: וְרָבָא — אֵין עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין, וְאַבַּיֵּי אָמַר לָךְ: הָא לָאו דִּינָא הוּא, מִי גָּרַע טוֹב מֵרַע?

a10.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ״ בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים, ״וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ״ בְּשֶׁל עַצְמוֹ. וְלִכְתּוֹב ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ״, וְלָא בָּעֵי ״לֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ״!

a11.he: אִי כְּתַב הָכִי — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: תֵּצֵא זוֹ וְתִכָּנֵס זוֹ הוּא דְּתִילְקֵי, אֲבָל מֵמִיר דְּתַרְוַויְיהוּ קָא מַקְדֵּישׁ לְהוּ — אֵימָא לָא לָקֵי. קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a12.he: הַאי בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי נֵימָא בְּהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ דִּידֵיהּ, וְחוּלִּין דְּעָלְמָא — מִי מָצֵי מַקְדֵּישׁ? ״אִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּישׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, מָה בֵּיתוֹ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, אַף כֹּל בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ. וְאֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ דְּעָלְמָא, וְחוּלִּין דִּידֵיהּ — מִי מַתְפֵּיס בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ?

a13.he: לְעוֹלָם בִּבְהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ דְּעָלְמָא, וְחוּלִּין דִּידֵיהּ, כְּגוֹן דְּאָמַר מָרֵיהּ דִּבְהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ: ״כׇּל הָרוֹצֶה לְהָמִיר בִּבְהֶמְתּוֹ יָבֹא וְיָמִיר״.

a14.he: מַתְנִי׳ מְמִירִין אֶחָד בִּשְׁנַיִם, וּשְׁנַיִם בְּאֶחָד, אֶחָד בְּמֵאָה, וּמֵאָה בְּאֶחָד. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְמִירִין אֶלָּא אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״, מָה ״הוּא״ מְיוּחָד, אַף הִיא מְיוּחֶדֶת.

a15.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה״ — מִכָּאן שֶׁמְּמִירִין אֶחָד בִּשְׁנַיִם, וּשְׁנַיִם בְּאֶחָד, אֶחָד בְּמֵאָה, וּמֵאָה בְּאֶחָד. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְמִירִין אֶלָּא אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה״, וְלֹא בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמוֹת, וְלֹא בְּהֵמוֹת בִּבְהֵמָה.

a16.he: אָמַר לוֹ: מָצִינוּ בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁקְּרוּיָה ״בְּהֵמָה״, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְהֵמָה רַבָּה״. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — ״בְּהֵמָה רַבָּה״ אִיקְּרִי, ״בְּהֵמָה״ סְתָם לָא אִיקְּרִי.

a17.he: וְטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִשּׁוּם ״בְּהֵמָה״ הוּא? וְהָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִשּׁוּם ״הוּא״, מָה ״הוּא״ מְיוּחָד — אַף תְּמוּרָה מְיוּחֶדֶת!

a18.he: מֵעִיקָּרָא אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִן ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ״, וְכִי חֲזָא דְּדָרְשִׁי רַבָּנַן מִ״בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה״, אָמַר לָהֶם אִיהוּ: מֵהָתָם נָמֵי מָצֵינַן לְמֵילַף טַעְמָא דִּידִי.

a19.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁמְּמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין, מַאי טַעְמָא? קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ לְהֵיכָן הָלְכָה?! וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מְמִירִין שְׁנַיִם בְּאֶחָד, כֵּן אֵין מְמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין.

a20.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מְמִירִין אֶחָד בִּשְׁנַיִם, כָּךְ אֵין מְמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין. תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: יָכוֹל כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁאֵין מְמִירִין שְׁנַיִם בְּאֶחָד, כָּךְ אֵין מְמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ״, אֲפִילּוּ בְּמֵאָה.

a21.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין: לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר ״אֵין מְמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין״, הִפְרִישׁ אָשָׁם לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בּוֹ, וְהֵמִיר בּוֹ,

b1.he: וְהוּמַם וְחִלְּלוֹ עַל אַחֵר, וְנִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק לְעוֹלָה — מַהוּ שֶׁיָּמִיר בּוֹ?

b2.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ? אִי שְׁנֵי גוּפִים וּקְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת — תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ בְּלֹא מִתְכַּפֵּר.

b3.he: אִי שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת, וְגוּף אֶחָד — תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ בְּלֹא הוּמַם!

b4.he: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר: שְׁנֵי גוּפִין וּקְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת — לָא, מִשּׁוּם דִּבְהָהִיא קְדוּשָּׁה הָא אִיתְּמַר בַּהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא. שְׁנֵי גוּפִין וּשְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת מַהוּ? תֵּיקוּ.

b5.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּאָמַר אֵין מְמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין — הִפְרִישׁ אָשָׁם לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בּוֹ, וְהֵמִיר בּוֹ, וְהוּמַם וְחִלְּלוֹ עַל אַחֵר, מַהוּ שֶׁיַּחְזוֹר וְיָמִיר?

b6.he: נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק זֶה לְעוֹלָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיַּחֲזִיר וְיָמִיר?

b7.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֵי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ? קְדוּשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת בְּאוֹתוֹ הַגּוּף — לָא נִיבְעֵי הוּמַם וְחִלְּלוֹ בְּאַחֵר! אִי גּוּף (אֶחָד) [אַחֵר] בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה — לָא נִיבְעֵי נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר!

b8.he: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: הוּמַם וְחִלְּלוֹ עַל אַחֵר, מַהוּ שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר וְיָמִיר? מִי אָמְרִינַן: בְּאָשָׁם רִאשׁוֹן הוּא דְּאֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר, אֲבָל בְּגוּף (אֶחָד) [אַחֵר], אַף עַל גַּב דְּקַדִּישׁ אוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה — חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר, אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֹּל בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה אֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר?

b9.he: וְאִם תִּימְצָא לוֹמַר הַדִּין גּוּף (אֶחָד) [אַחֵר], כֵּיוָן דִּבְאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה קָאֵים — אֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר, אֶלָּא נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק זֶה רִאשׁוֹן לְעוֹלָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיַּחֲזִיר וְיָמִיר בּוֹ?

b10.he: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כִּי אֵין מֵמִיר וְחוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר — הָנֵי מִילֵּי אוֹתוֹ הַגּוּף בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה, אֲבָל אוֹתוֹ הַגּוּף בִּקְדוּשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת — חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר, אוֹ דִלְמָא: אַף עַל קְדוּשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת, כֵּיוָן דְּאוֹתוֹ הַגּוּף הוּא — אֵין חוֹזֵר וּמֵמִיר? תֵּיקוּ.

b11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֶקְדֵּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ, וְאֵין הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֵׁנִי מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.

b12.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם הַמַּקְדִּישׁ יִגְאַל אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית״ — מַקְדִּישׁ, וְלֹא הַמַּתְפִּיס.

b13.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין: הִפְרִישׁ אָשָׁם לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בּוֹ, וְהוּמַם, וְהוֹסִיף עָלָיו חוֹמֶשׁ, וְחִלְּלוֹ חֲבֵירוֹ, וְנִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק זֶה לְעוֹלָה — מַהוּ שֶׁיּוֹסִיף עָלָיו חוֹמֶשׁ?

b14.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ? אִי שְׁנֵי גוּפִין וּקְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ — תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ בְּלֹא נִתְכַּפֵּר!

b15.he: אִי שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת, וְגוּף אֶחָד קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ — תִּיבְּעֵי בְּלֹא הוּמַם!

b16.he: וְרַבִּי אָבִין, חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: אִם תִּימְצָא לוֹמַר שְׁנֵי גוּפִין וּקְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת לָא — מִשּׁוּם דִּבְהָהִיא קְדוּשָּׁה אִיתּוֹסַף בַּהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא חוֹמֶשׁ, שְׁנֵי גוּפִין וּשְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת מַאי? תֵּיקוּ.

b17.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין: הִפְרִישׁ אָשָׁם לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בּוֹ, וְהוּמַם וְחִלְּלוֹ עַל אַחֵר וְהוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ, נִתְכַּפְּרוּ בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק זֶה לְעוֹלָה — מַהוּ שֶׁיּוֹסִיף עָלָיו חוֹמֶשׁ?

b18.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָדֵין קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, אִי קְדוּשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת בְּאוֹתוֹ הַגּוּף קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ — לָא נִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ הוּמַם, אִי גּוּף (אֶחָד) [אַחֵר] בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה כּוּ׳.

b19.he: וְחִלְּלוֹ עַל אַחֵר, מַהוּ שֶׁיּוֹסִיף עָלָיו חוֹמֶשׁ? מִי אָמְרִינַן: בְּאָשָׁם קַמָּא הוּא דְּמוֹסֵיף, אֲבָל בְּגוּף (אֶחָד) [אַחֵר], אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָאֵים בְּאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה, [אֵין] מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ,

messages.text: 9a

Continued from 8b: at Rav Ashi’s home, Mar Zutra questioned his hosts about eating a firstborn bought from a priest. In the alternative version of their answer, they paid for it, and there is no concern that the priest lowered the price hoping to receive their future firstborns, as he thinks:
A zucchini now is better than the possibility of a gourd later. There is no reason to give up an animal now for the hope of receiving another later.
Mishna

It is written: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good; and if he substitutes an animal for an animal, then both it and its substitute shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:10). The mishna enumerates the consecrated and non-sacred animals this verse applies to.

One substitutes for consecrated animals from the flock of sheep or goats, and the sanctity takes effect upon animals from the herd of cattle, and one substitutes from the herd and the sanctity takes effect upon animals from the flock. And one substitutes from the sheep and the sanctity takes effect upon the goats, and from the goats upon the sheep; and from the males upon the females, and from the females upon the males; and from the unblemished animals upon the blemished animals, and from the blemished animals upon the unblemished animals.

notes.he: תמים של חולין לא יתפיס ברע של קדש ואם המר ימיר וגו' אלמא בעלי מומין עבדי תמורה. ואבעל מום חיילא תמורה דכתיב או רע בטוב דמשמע בעל מום דחולין בתם דהקדש:
notes.en: Mishna. Good for bad: one may not apply [the sanctity of] an unblemished non-sacred animal to a bad [blemished] consecrated one, and yet “if he substitutes” etc. Evidently blemished animals effect substitution. And substitution takes effect upon a blemished animal, as it is written: “or bad for good,” which means a blemished non-sacred animal for an unblemished consecrated one.

notes.he: של חולין על בעלי מומין של קדשים:
notes.en: From the unblemished: non-sacred animals, upon the blemished consecrated animals.

notes.he: של חולין על תמימין של קדשים שנאמר לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו טוב ברע או רע בטוב:
notes.en: From the blemished: non-sacred animals, upon unblemished consecrated animals, as it is stated: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good.”

messages.text: The source for this is as it is stated: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good.” And which is the case of good for bad where the substitution takes effect? It is a case where one substitutes for blemished animals whose consecration preceded their blemish. But if an animal was consecrated after it was blemished, substitution for it does not take effect.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: כלומר איזהו רע דקדש דעביד תמורה שקדם הקדשו את מומו אבל קדם מומו את הקדשו לא עביד תמורה. ובגמרא מפרש מאי תלמודא:
notes.en: And which is good for bad: that is to say, which bad consecrated animal effects substitution? One whose consecration preceded its blemish; but if its blemish preceded its consecration, it does not effect substitution. And the Gemara explains what the derivation is.

notes.dh: שנאמר לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו טוב ברע או רע בטוב
notes.he: טוב קודש ברע דחולין או רע דקדש בטוב דחולין זה הכלל הראשון הוא הקדש:
notes.en: As it is stated: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good”: a good consecrated animal for a bad non-sacred one, or a bad consecrated animal for a good non-sacred one. This is the rule: the first [named] is the consecrated one.

notes.dh: איזהו טוב ברע בעלי מומין שקדם הקדישן למומן
notes.he: זהו הפך מן האחרים שהרי הכא האחד הוא הנתפס:
notes.en: And which is good for bad? Blemished animals whose consecration preceded their blemish: this is the reverse of the others, for here the first [named] is the one taken [into sanctity, i.e., the non-sacred animal].

notes.he: תם של חולין ברע של קדשים מנלן דבעל מום איקרי רע דכתיב כל מום רע היינו שקדם הקדישן את מומן כדמפרש בגמרא [ומן תמימין של חולין על בעלי מומין של קדשים יכול אפי' קדם מום קבוע להקדישן ת"ל כו':
notes.en: And which is good for bad: an unblemished non-sacred animal for a bad consecrated one. From where do we know that a blemished animal is called “bad”? As it is written: “any bad blemish” (Deuteronomy 15:21). That is, where their consecration preceded their blemish, as is explained in the Gemara. [And from unblemished non-sacred animals upon blemished consecrated animals: one might have thought, even where a permanent blemish preceded their consecration; the verse states etc.]

messages.text: Gemara
From where are these matters derived? They are derived from a verse, as the Sages taught in a baraita:

The verse states: “And if he substitutes an animal for an animal, then both it and its substitute shall be sacred.” When the verse states: “An animal for an animal,” from here it is derived that one substitutes for consecrated animals from the flock and the sanctity takes effect upon animals from the herd, and one likewise substitutes from the herd upon animals from the flock; and one substitutes from the sheep and the sanctity takes effect upon the goats, and from the goats upon the sheep; and from the males upon the females and from the females upon the males; and from the blemished animals upon the unblemished animals and from the unblemished animals upon the blemished animals.

One might have thought that this is the halakha even for animals whose blemish preceded their consecration. Therefore, the verse states: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good,” and which is the case of good for bad where the substitution takes effect? It is a case of blemished animals whose consecration preceded their blemish. If an animal was consecrated after it was blemished, substitution for it does not take effect.

notes.dh: איזהו טוב של חולין ברע של קדשים
notes.he: באותו שקדם הקדשו למומו]:
notes.en: Which is a good non-sacred animal for a bad consecrated one: one whose consecration preceded its blemish.

messages.text: The Gemara discusses the second half of the baraita: What is the biblical derivation that leads to this conclusion?

The verse should have stated: He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for it. Why do I need another instance of the term “for good”? Learn from this repetition that if the animal is good, i.e., unblemished, from its beginning, before it was consecrated, one can render a substitute for it, but if it is bad from its beginning, one cannot render a substitute for it.

notes.dh: גמ' נכתוב לא ימיר אותו טוב ברע או רע בו
notes.he: והוי משמע או רע לא ימיר לא בטוב ולא ברע:
notes.en: Gemara. Let the verse write: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for it”: and it would mean: or a bad one he shall not substitute, neither for a good one nor for a bad one.

notes.dh: בטוב בתרא ל"ל לומר לך טוב מעיקרו
notes.he: שבשעה שהוקדש היה תמים ושוב נפל בו מום עושה תמורה:
notes.en: Why do I need the latter “for good”? To tell you: good from its beginning, that at the time it was consecrated it was unblemished and afterward a blemish befell it, effects substitution.

notes.he: ולרבא תרוייהו דהוה מצי למכתב ולא ימיר אותו ברע או רע וקשה מההיא דפ"ב דבכורות (דף יד:) דאמר השתא רע דקדש בטוב דחולין אמרת לא טוב דקדש ברע דחולין מיבעיא משמע דטוב ברע מיותר למעוטי היכא דקדם מומן להקדישן דלא מתפיסין בתמורה ואין זה לא כאביי ולא כרבא ועוד קשה מאי קאמר טוב ברע מיבעיא והא איצטריך למימר דנתפס רע דחולין בטוב דקדש ויש לומר דהתם הכי קאמר לכתוב רחמנא ולא ימיר אותו רע בטוב או ברע טוב ברע למה לי כלומר טוב ל"ל אבל לא קאמר דנישתוק מטוב ברע כו' אלא מטוב לבד והיינו כאביי:
notes.en: According to Abaye one “good” is superfluous, and according to Rava both are, as the verse could have written: “nor substitute it for bad, or bad for it.” And this is difficult in light of the passage in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14b), which says: Now, a bad consecrated animal for a good non-sacred one, you said [substitution takes effect]; a good consecrated animal for a bad non-sacred one, is it necessary? This implies that “good for bad” is superfluous, to exclude a case where their blemish preceded their consecration, that they are not taken in substitution; and this is neither like Abaye nor like Rava. And it is further difficult: what does it mean, “good for bad, is it necessary”? It was necessary, to say that a bad non-sacred animal is taken for a good consecrated one! And one can say that there it means this: Let the Merciful One write: “nor substitute it, bad for good, or for bad”; why do I need “good for bad,” that is, why do I need “good”? But it does not say that the verse should omit “good for bad” entirely, only “good” alone, and this is like Abaye.

notes.he: היכי משמע מהכא מדשני קרא ואמר בטוב דלא איצטריך דניכתוב קרא טוב ברע או רע ולא לימא בטוב דכיון דקא' או רע [היינו] משמע בטוב ואמאי אמר תו בטוב אלא טוב מעיקרא עושה תמורה היינו שקדם הקדשו למומו [ולא רע מעקרו דהיינו שקדם מומו]:
notes.en: Gemara. What is the derivation: how is it implied from here [that it speaks of where their consecration preceded their blemish]? From the fact that the verse departed [from its pattern] and said “for good,” which was not needed: let the verse write “good for bad, or bad,” and not say “for good,” since once it says “or bad” that already implies “for good.” So why does it say “for good” again? Rather: good from its beginning effects substitution, that is, where its consecration preceded its blemish, [and not bad from its beginning, that is, where its blemish preceded].

messages.text: Both instances of the word “good” in the verse are superfluous. If so, let the verse write: He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it for bad, or bad for it. Why do I need the verse to write both instances of the word “good”?

notes.he: והוי משמע דאיהו הוי טוב:
notes.en: He shall not substitute it for bad: and it would imply that it [the consecrated animal] is good.

notes.he: משמע או רע של חולין לא ימיר בטוב:
notes.en: Or bad: implies: or a bad non-sacred animal he shall not substitute for a good [consecrated] one.

messages.text: One instance of the word “good” teaches that even if one substitutes a good animal for a good animal, when he effects substitution he is flogged. And the other instance teaches that if the animal is good from its beginning one can render a substitute for it, but if it is bad from its beginning one cannot render a substitute for it.

notes.dh: רבא אמר מתרוייהו טוב מצי ילפת
notes.he: דתרוייהו מייתרי (רי"ח) [אלא] חד טוב אתא [דאפילו] טוב בטוב לא ימיר [דאין אדם רשאי להמיר] וחד בטוב לטוב מעיקרא כו' [קל וחומר הוא רע של קדשים בטוב דחולין דקא מפיק רע דקודש ומייתי טוב בחולין במקומו לא ימיר. טוב בטוב דכי הדדי ננהו דלא קא מעלי ליה כ"ש דלקי]:
notes.en: Rava said: You can derive from both instances of “good,” for both are superfluous. [Rather,] one “good” comes [to teach that even] good for good he shall not substitute, [as a person is not permitted to substitute], and one “for good” teaches about good from its beginning etc. [The a fortiori inference: a bad consecrated animal for a good non-sacred one, where he takes out the bad consecrated animal and brings a good non-sacred one in its place, he shall not substitute; good for good, which are equal, where he does not improve it, all the more so is he flogged.]

messages.text: The first derivation of Rava is unnecessary, as that halakha is already derived by an a fortiori inference, as follows: Just as one who substitutes a good animal for a bad blemished one, where he seeks to improve the standing of the consecrated animal by making it fit for sacrifice, is nevertheless flogged, is it not all the more so the case that one who substitutes a good animal for a good animal, which are equivalent to each other, should be flogged?
messages.quote: Why do I need the verse to write both instances of the word “good”?

notes.he: טוב של חולין ברע של קדש:
notes.en: Good for bad: a good non-sacred animal for a bad consecrated one.

notes.he: להקדש לקי טוב בטוב מיבעיא:
notes.en: Where he improves it: he improves the consecrated property, and he is flogged; good for good, is it even necessary [to state]?

messages.text: And Rava would respond that an a fortiori inference is not sufficient, as one does not administer punishment based on an a fortiori inference. Punishment with lashes can be based only on the explicit wording of a verse.

notes.he: ולהכי איצטריך קרא דמשום דין קל וחומר לא מלקינן ליה כי מימר טוב בטוב:
notes.en: One does not administer punishment on the basis of an a fortiori inference: and therefore the verse was needed, since on account of an a fortiori inference alone we would not flog him when he substitutes good for good.

messages.text: And Abaye could say to you that this is not a mere logical derivation, but it is included in the language of the verse, as, is substituting a good, unblemished, animal less of an act of substitution than substituting a bad one? The prohibition stated in the verse clearly applies in either case.

notes.dh: ואביי אמר לך האי לאו עונשין מן הדין הוא אלא אגלויי מילתא בעלמא היא
notes.he: דהיכא דגלי קרא דלקי אטוב דחולין כי מימר ליה ברע דקדש גלי נמי דאי מימר ליה בטוב דקדש לקי:
notes.en: And Abaye could say to you: This is not punishing on the basis of an inference; rather it merely reveals the matter: where the verse revealed that he is flogged for a good non-sacred animal when he substitutes it for a bad consecrated one, it also revealed that if he substitutes it for a good consecrated one, he is flogged.

notes.he: כלומר מי גרע טוב דקדש מרע דקדש כי היכי דרע דקדש כי מחליף ליה לקי ה"ה לטוב דקדש דרחמנא לא קפיד אלא דלא יחליף מידי דקדש:
notes.en: For is good less than bad: that is to say, is a good consecrated animal less than a bad consecrated animal? Just as with a bad consecrated animal, when he exchanges it he is flogged, the same is true of a good consecrated animal, as the Merciful One is concerned only that he not exchange anything consecrated.

notes.he: סבר גלויי מילתא בעלמא הואיל ולקי על האי [לקי גם אהאי] לישנא אחרינא לאו דינא הוא אלא ממילא מצית ילפת דמי גרע טוב לרע (דכתיב לא יבקר בין טוב לרע) דקא מעלי ליה דלקי טפי מטוב בטוב דלא קא מעלי ליה ולא לקי אלא ש"מ דטוב בטוב נמי לקי אע"ג דלא כתב ביה [לאו]:
notes.en: And Abaye holds that it merely reveals the matter: since he is flogged for this, [he is flogged for that too]. Another version: it is not a logical inference; rather you can derive it of itself, for is good less than bad (as it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad,” Leviticus 27:33), where he improves it, so that he should be flogged more than for good for good, where he does not improve it, and not be flogged? Rather, learn from this that for good for good he is also flogged, even though [a prohibition] is not written about it. [The text here is uncertain; an editor’s note proposes a corrected reading along these lines.]

messages.text: § The Sages taught in a baraita:

When the verse states: “He shall neither exchange it,” this is referring to substituting one’s animal for that of others. The phrase “nor substitute it” is referring to substituting one’s non-sacred animal for his own sacred one.

notes.he: חולין של אחרים ולא ימיר אותו (בשל הקדש) [בחולין] של עצמו:
notes.en: For that of others: the non-sacred animal of others. And “nor substitute it”: with his own non-sacred animal.

messages.text: But let the verse write simply: “He shall not exchange it,” and there will be no need to write: “Nor substitute it,” as the prohibition against substituting for one’s own animal can be inferred a fortiori from the prohibition against substituting for another’s animal.

notes.he: חילוף משמע ע"י ב' אנשים ולא בעי ולא ימיר דמי גרע של עצמו משל אחרים:
notes.en: Exchanging implies [an act] by two people. And there would be no need for “nor substitute it,” for is [substituting for] one’s own less than [for] another’s?

messages.text: If the verse had written the prohibition in that manner, I would say that one is flogged only if he stated: This consecrated animal should leave its consecrated status and this non-sacred animal should enter in its stead.

notes.he: והתם אע"ג דלא אהני מידי דהקדש תם אינו יוצא לחולין אפ"ה לילקי הואיל ונתכוין להוציא הקדש לחולין:
notes.en: Exchanging is “this goes out and this comes in”: and there, even though he accomplished nothing, since an unblemished consecrated animal does not go out to non-sacred status, he is nevertheless flogged, since he intended to take consecrated property out to non-sacred status.

notes.he: לא יחליפנו דמשמע בשל אחרים:
notes.en: If it had written: “He shall not exchange it,” which implies [substituting] for that of others:

notes.dh: הוה אמינא תצא זו ותכנס זו הוא דלקי
notes.he: שלוקח בהמת חברו ונותן לו זו ומוציא האחרת לחולין:
notes.en: I would say that it is for “this should leave and this should enter” that he is flogged: that he takes his fellow’s animal, gives him this one, and takes the other out to non-sacred status.

messages.text: But if one effects substitution by simply stating: This is a substitute for that, as he has consecrated both of the animals, I would say that he is not flogged. The additional phrase in the verse teaches us that he is flogged in this case as well.

notes.he: בשל עצמו:
notes.en: But one who effects substitution: with his own.

notes.dh: דתרווייהו מצי מקדיש להו אימא לא לקי
notes.he: אלא לקדיש לתרווייהו וליפטר קמ"ל דלא אלא לקי:
notes.en: As he has consecrated both of them, I would say he is not flogged: rather, let both be consecrated and let him be exempt. It teaches us that this is not so, but he is flogged.

messages.text: What are the circumstances of substituting his animal for that of others? If we say that the consecrated animal is his and the non-sacred animal belongs to others, is he able to consecrate an animal in this manner? The Merciful One states in the Torah: “When a man shall consecrate his house to be sacred unto the Lord,” which teaches that just as his house is in his possession, so too, any item one desires to consecrate must be in his possession. One cannot consecrate another’s animal.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת־בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יָקוּם׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who consecrates a house to GOD: The priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, as the priest assesses it, so it shall stand;

messages.text: But rather, if we say that the consecrated animal belongs to others, and the non-sacred animal is his, can one effect substitution for an item that is not his?

Actually, the baraita is referring to a consecrated animal of others and his non-sacred animal, and it is a case where the owner of the consecrated animal said that whoever wants to effect substitution for his animal can come and effect substitution. In this case, one can effect substitution even for a consecrated item that is not his.
messages.quote: What are the circumstances of substituting his animal for that of others?

messages.text: Mishna

One substitutes one non-sacred animal for two consecrated animals and two non-sacred animals for one consecrated animal, and one substitutes one non-sacred animal for one hundred consecrated animals and one hundred non-sacred animals for one consecrated animal.

notes.he: של חולין:
notes.en: Mishna. One substitutes one: non-sacred animal.

notes.he: דקדש ואומר הרי זו תחת אלו:
notes.en: For two: consecrated animals, and he says: This is in place of these.

notes.he: דחולין באחד דקדש הרי אלו תחת זו:
notes.en: And two: non-sacred animals for one consecrated animal: These are in place of this one.

messages.text: One substitutes only one non-sacred animal for one consecrated animal, as it is stated: “Then both it and its substitute shall be sacred.” Just as “it” indicates one specific animal, so too, its substitute can be only one specific animal.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: דכתיב הוא:
notes.en: Just as “it” is specific: for it is written “it” [hu].

messages.text: Gemara
With regard to the dispute between the first tanna and Rabbi Shimon, the Gemara explains: From where are these matters derived? As the Sages taught in a baraita:

The verse states: “An animal for an animal.” From here it is derived that one substitutes one non-sacred animal for two consecrated animals and two non-sacred animals for one consecrated animal, and one non-sacred animal for one hundred consecrated animals and one hundred non-sacred animals for one consecrated animal.

One substitutes only one non-sacred animal for one consecrated animal, as it is stated: “An animal [behema] for an animal,” and it is not stated: An animal for animals [bivehemot], nor: Animals for an animal.
We have found that a group of animals is called by the singular term behema, as it is stated: “And many animals [uvhema rabba].”

verse.he: וַאֲנִי לֹא אָחוּס עַל־נִינְוֵה הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה אֲשֶׁר יֶשׁ־בָּהּ הַרְבֵּה מִשְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵה רִבּוֹ אָדָם אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יָדַע בֵּין־יְמִינוֹ לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ וּבְהֵמָה רַבָּה׃
verse.en: And should not I care about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not yet know their right hand from their left, and many animals as well!”

messages.text: And Rabbi Shimon could respond that many animals are indeed called “behema rabba,” but they are not called “behema” without further specification.

And is the reason of Rabbi Shimon really due to the verse’s phrase “an animal for an animal”? But isn’t the reason of Rabbi Shimon, as explained in the mishna, due to the word “it” in the verse? Just as “it” indicates one specific animal, so too, its substitute can be only one specific animal.
messages.quote: Just as “it” indicates one specific animal

notes.he: במתניתין משום האי קרא הוא דוהיה הוא ותמורתו:
notes.en: Gemara. But isn’t the reason of Rabbi Shimon: in our mishna, due to this verse: “Then both it and its substitute”?

notes.he: והא טעמא דרבי שמעון משום הוא הוי אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש מודה רבי שמעון דממירין וחוזרין וממירין - ופרש"י ללשון ראשון דתירוץ הוא ומשום הכי אתא בהמה בבהמה ודוחק הוא דאדרבה לדברי רבי שמעון משמע דבהמה חדא משמע ולא שנים והיכי קאמר דמפיק מיניה דממירין וחוזרין וממירין ול"א פרש"י דגרס מעיקרא אמר להן רבי שמעון מוהיה הוא ותמורתו וכי חזא דדרשי רבנן מבהמה בבהמה אמר להון איהו מהתם נמי מצי למילף טעמא דידי ורשב"ל מימרא דנפשיה קאמר ולאו לתרוצי הך פירכא אתא:
notes.en: But isn’t the reason of Rabbi Shimon due to “it”? … Reish Lakish says: Rabbi Shimon concedes that one can effect substitution and then effect substitution again: Rashi explained, according to the first version, that this is an answer, and that is why “an animal for an animal” comes [to teach repeated substitution]. And this is forced, for on the contrary, according to Rabbi Shimon “an animal” implies one and not two; how then does he say that one derives from it that one substitutes and then substitutes again? And in another version Rashi explained that he reads: “Initially, Rabbi Shimon stated to them from ‘then both it and its substitute,’ and when he saw that the Rabbis expounded ‘an animal for an animal,’ he said to them: From there too I can derive my reason”; and Reish Lakish states his own statement and did not come to answer that objection.

notes.he: בהמה ולא בהמות כו':
notes.en: [And the reason of Rabbi Shimon is due to “an animal,” and not animals etc.:

messages.text: Initially, Rabbi Shimon stated his opinion to the Sages by drawing support from the phrase: “Then both it and its substitute.” But when he saw that the Rabbis taught their opinion drawing support from the phrase “an animal for an animal,”

notes.he: ל"א מעיקרא במתניתין אהדר להו מן והיה הוא וגו' ובברייתא דבעו רבנן למילף מן בהמה בבהמה אמר להו אדרבה בבהמה בבהמה לא משמע אלא אחד באחד. ולהאי לישנא אמר ריש לקיש הוי ריש מימרא]:
notes.en: Another version: initially, in the mishna, he answered them from “then both it” etc., and in the baraita, where the Rabbis sought to derive from “an animal for an animal,” he said to them: On the contrary, “an animal for an animal” implies only one for one. And according to this version, Reish Lakish is the beginning of a [new] statement.]

messages.text: You can learn the reason for my opinion from there too.

Rashi’s first reading has no such answer here: the question is answered by Reish Lakish’s statement that follows. He also records the reading printed here, in which Reish Lakish makes a separate statement of his own (see his notes on Reish Lakish, and Tosafot on the question).

Although he holds that one cannot substitute two animals for one, Rabbi Shimon concedes that one can effect substitution once and then effect substitution again for the same consecrated animal. What is the reason for this? The reason is that one can ask: Where has the initial consecration of the consecrated animal gone? Even after one effects substitution, it remains consecrated as it was before.

notes.dh: ומשנינן אמר ר' שמעון בן לקיש מודה רבי שמעון שממירין וחוזרין וממירין
notes.he: בהמה אחרת באותה בהמה ראשונה דהקדיש ואפילו עד מאה:
notes.en: And we answer: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Rabbi Shimon concedes that one substitutes and then substitutes again: another animal for that same first animal that he consecrated, even up to a hundred. [In this reading, Reish Lakish’s statement is the answer to the question just asked.]

notes.dh: מאי טעמא דקדושה ראשונה דהקדש ראשון להיכן הלכה
notes.he: שלא יתפיס עוד אחרת בקדושתו עד אלף. לשון אחר אמר רבי דגרסינן מעיקרא אמר להן רבי שמעון מן והיה הוא ותמורתו וכי חזא דדרשי רבנן מבהמה בבהמה אמר להן איהו מהתם נמי מצינא למילף טעמא דידי ור' שמעון בן לקיש מימרא דנפשיה קאמר ולא לתרוצי הך פירכא אתא:
notes.en: What is the reason? Where has the initial sanctity of the first consecration gone? [It remains,] so that he can apply yet another animal to its sanctity, even up to a thousand. Another version, which my teacher said: we read [the text]: “Initially, Rabbi Shimon stated to them from ‘then both it and its substitute,’ and when he saw that the Rabbis expounded ‘an animal for an animal,’ he said to them: From there too I can derive my reason.” And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish states his own statement, and did not come to answer that objection.

notes.he: אע"ג דאמר ר' שמעון אין מימר אלא אחד באחד מודה ר' שמעון שממירין וחוזרין וממירין באותה בהמת הקדש אפילו מאה אחד באחד בזה אחר זה וקא יליף האי סברא מן בהמה בבהמה ולא בהמה בבהמות הרבה ביחד אבל על בהמה אחת ממירין וחוזרין וממירין בזה אחר זה בהמות הרבה דהיינו נמי אחד באחד:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish said: Even though Rabbi Shimon said one substitutes only one for one, Rabbi Shimon concedes that one substitutes and then substitutes again with that same consecrated animal, even a hundred, one for one, one after the other. And he derives this reasoning from “an animal for an animal,” and not an animal for many animals together; but for one animal one substitutes and then substitutes again, many animals one after the other, since this too is one for one.

notes.he: דהא כתיב הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש:
notes.en: The initial sanctity, where has it gone? For it is written: “Both it and its substitute shall be sacred.”

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon maintains that just as one cannot substitute two animals for one, so too, one cannot effect substitution and then effect substitution again using the same consecrated animal.
messages.quote: Rabbi Shimon concedes that one can effect substitution once and then effect substitution again

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, and it is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Reish Lakish.
Just as one cannot substitute one animal for two, so too, one cannot effect substitution and then effect substitution again.
messages.lead: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
messages.quote: cannot effect substitution and then effect substitution again

messages.text: One might have thought that just as Rabbi Shimon said that one cannot substitute two animals for one, so too, one cannot effect substitution and then effect substitution again. Therefore, the verse states: “Then both it and its substitute,” which teaches that one can effect substitution with even one hundred non-sacred animals.
messages.lead: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Reish Lakish:
messages.quote: Rabbi Shimon concedes that one can effect substitution once and then effect substitution again

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

messages.text: According to the statement of the one who says that one cannot effect substitution once and then effect substitution again, if one designated an animal as a guilt offering with which to atone and effected substitution for it,

notes.dh: [לדברי האומר אין ממירין וחוזרין וממירין הפריש אשם להתכפר בו והמיר בו
notes.he: בהמה אחת. והומם האשם וחיללו על אחר. ונאבד אותו שחילל עליו והביא אשם אחד ונכפר בו ואח"כ נמצא אותו שנאבד וניתק לעולה:
notes.en: [According to the one who says one cannot substitute and then substitute again: he designated a guilt offering to atone with it and substituted one animal for it; and the guilt offering became blemished and he desacralized it onto another; and the one onto which he desacralized it was lost, and he brought another guilt offering and achieved atonement with it; and afterward the one that was lost was found and consigned to a burnt offering:

messages.text: 9b

and the original guilt offering became blemished, and he desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another animal, which was then lost, and the owner achieved atonement by bringing another, third, animal as a guilt offering, and then the second animal was found and was consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, as is the case for any guilt offering whose owner has achieved atonement by means of another offering, what is the halakha as to whether he can effect substitution for the second animal?

notes.he: הראשון:
notes.en: And it became blemished: the first one.

notes.dh: וחיללו על אחר ונתכפר באשם אחר
notes.he: אחר שאבד אשם שני זה שחילל הראשון עליו ונתכפר באחר ואח"כ נמצא זה:
notes.en: And he desacralized it onto another, and achieved atonement with another guilt offering: after this second guilt offering, onto which he had desacralized the first, was lost, he achieved atonement with another, and afterward this one was found.

notes.he: דאשם שכיפרו בעליו באחר סתמיה לשם עולת נדבת צבור קאי דהיינו מן המותרות דמדרש יהוידע הכהן בפ' ולד חטאת (לקמן תמורה דף כג:):
notes.en: And it was consigned to a burnt offering: for a guilt offering whose owner achieved atonement with another stands, without specification, as a communal voluntary burnt offering, that is, from the surplus, as Yehoyada the priest expounded, in the chapter Velad Ḥattat (below, Temurah 23b).

notes.he: מי אמרינן כיון דמכח קמא אתא אין ממירין בו דהא המיר בראשון או דלמא כיון דגופא אחרינא הוא וקדושה אחריתי היא דכי המיר בקמא הוה אשם והאי הוה עולה הלכך ממירין:
notes.en: What is the halakha as to whether he can substitute for it: do we say that since it comes by force of the first one, one does not substitute for it, as he already substituted for the first? Or perhaps, since it is another body and another sanctity, for when he substituted for the first it was a guilt offering and this one is a burnt offering, he therefore can substitute?

notes.he: דהשתא איכא ב' גופין וב' קדושות דמעיקרא הפריש אשם דהיינו קדושה אחת וגוף אחד והימר בו והומם וחיללו על אחר וניתק זה לעולה היינו קדושה אחריתי וגוף אחר:
notes.en: What is the halakha as to whether he can substitute for it: for now there are two bodies and two sanctities. Initially he designated a guilt offering, which is one sanctity and one body, and substituted for it; and it became blemished and he desacralized it onto another, and this one was consigned to a burnt offering, which is another sanctity and another body.

messages.text: Since this animal’s sanctity stems from that of the original blemished animal, and he had already effected a substitute for that original animal, perhaps he cannot now substitute for the second animal, as this would constitute repeat substitution.

messages.caption: Rabbi Avin’s guilt offering: the same animal or another, the same sanctity or another, and which case each version of his dilemma asks about.

messages.text: What is the dilemma he is raising? If his essential dilemma concerns the fact that there are two bodies, i.e., two different animals, then the dilemma would stand even if the original animal and the replacement were of one type of sanctity. If so, let the dilemma be raised even in a case where he did not achieve atonement by another guilt offering, and the second animal remained a guilt offering, rather than being consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering.
messages.quote: a guilt offering with which to atone and effected substitution for it

notes.dh: אי שני גופין וקדושה אחת מיבעיא ליה
notes.he: דמי אמרינן כיון דגופא אחרינא הוה מימר או דלמא כיון דקדושה אחת היא לא מימר:
notes.en: If he raises a dilemma about two bodies and one sanctity: do we say that since it is another body he can substitute, or perhaps since it is one sanctity he cannot substitute?

notes.dh: אי הכי מיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא נתכפר
notes.he: דהכי איבעי ליה למימר הפריש אשם להתכפר בו והמיר בו והומם הראשון וחיללו על אחר מהו שימיר בזה האחר כיון דגופא אחרינא הוא מימר או דלמא כיון דמכח קמא אתא וחדא קדושה דקמא הוה אשם והאי נמי אשם לא מימר ולמה לי למימר נתכפר באחר:
notes.en: If so, let the dilemma be raised without atonement: for this is how he should have phrased it: he designated a guilt offering to atone with it and substituted for it, and the first became blemished and he desacralized it onto another; what is the halakha as to whether he can substitute for this other one? Since it is another body he can substitute; or perhaps, since it comes by force of the first and it is one sanctity, the first being a guilt offering and this one also a guilt offering, he cannot substitute. Why then do I need to say that he achieved atonement with another?

notes.dh: ומאי קא מיבעיא ליה אי ב' גופין וקדושה אחת
notes.he: אם ממירין וחוזרין וממירין באותן ב' גופין בקדושה אחת:
notes.en: And what is he asking? If two bodies and one sanctity: whether one substitutes and then substitutes again with those two bodies in one sanctity.

messages.text: And if the dilemma is due to the fact that there are two types of sanctity, it would stand even if it was only one body. If so, let the dilemma be raised even where the animal did not become blemished but was simply lost and found after the owner atoned by means of another animal, and it was thereby consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering. Why did Rabbi Avin present such a complex case?

notes.he: קא מיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא הומם וחיללו והכי ליתני הפריש אשם והמיר בו ואבד הראשון ונתכפר באשם אחר שהפריש מעדרו ונמצא הראשון וניתק לעולה דהוה ליה גוף אחד ושתי קדושות מהו מי אמר כיון דחד גופא הוא דמספקא ליה ולהכי קא מתמה אמאי קתני תרתי:
notes.en: And if two sanctities and one body: is what he is asking, let him ask it without its becoming blemished and his desacralizing it. And this is how he should teach it: he designated a guilt offering and substituted for it, and the first was lost, and he achieved atonement with another guilt offering that he designated from his flock, and the first was found and consigned to a burnt offering, so that it is one body and two sanctities; what is the halakha? Do we say: since it is one body…? For this is what he is uncertain about. And that is why he wonders why [Rabbi Avin] taught two [elements].

notes.he: וליבעי הכי הפריש אשם להתכפר בו והמיר בו והומם וחיללו על אחר מהו לחזור ולהמיר. באותו אחר דהאי אחר היינו גוף אחר באותה קדושה עצמה דאשם ואי ב' קדושות וגוף אחר קא מיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא הומם וליבעי הכי הפריש אשם להתכפר בו והמיר בו ונאבד האשם ונתכפר באשם אחד ואח"כ נמצא הראשון וניתק זה לעולה דהיינו אותו גוף עצמו בקדושה אחרת דעולה הוי השתא מהו שיחזור וימיר באותו גוף עצמו בקדושה אחרת:
notes.en: Let him ask it without atonement: let him ask thus: he designated a guilt offering to atone with it, and substituted for it, and it became blemished and he desacralized it onto another; what is the halakha as to substituting again with that other one? For that other one is another body in the very same sanctity of a guilt offering. And if he is asking about two sanctities and [one] body, let him ask it without the blemish; let him ask thus: he designated a guilt offering to atone with it, and substituted for it, and the guilt offering was lost, and he achieved atonement with another guilt offering, and afterward the first was found and was consigned to a burnt offering, which is that very same body in another sanctity, since now it is a burnt offering; what is the halakha as to whether he can substitute again with that same body in another sanctity?

messages.text: Rabbi Avin raises one dilemma as a result of the anticipated solution to another dilemma: If you say that in the case of two bodies and one type of sanctity it is not possible to effect substitution on the second animal, perhaps that is because this sanctity already had been substituted one time. If so, what is the halakha in the case of two bodies and two types of sanctity? Is the offering changed enough to enable another substitution for it?

notes.he: כלומר אם תמצא לומר קאמר וחדא בעיא היא והכי קאמר הפריש אשם והמיר בו והומם וחיללו דהוה ליה האי גוף שני וקדושה אחת מהו:
notes.en: One from within another: that is to say, he is saying “if you say,” and it is one dilemma, and this is what he says: he designated a guilt offering and substituted for it, and it became blemished and he desacralized it, so that this is a second body and one sanctity; what is the halakha?

notes.he: הכא כיון דקדושה אחת היא אינו מימר (משום דבההיא קדושה) איתמר בה ואינו מימר בה פעם אחרת:
notes.en: And if you say: here, since it is one sanctity, he cannot substitute, because with that sanctity he already substituted, and he does not substitute with it another time.

notes.he: כגון אבד שני זה מתכפר באחר ושני ניתק לעולה כשנמצא מהו כיון דהשתא שני הוא וקדושה אחרת היא מימר או דלמא סוף סוף מכח קמא אתא ואינו מימר. בלישנא אחרינא ירושלמי גרסי' לה ותרתי קבעי הפריש אשם והמיר בו והומם וחיללו על אחר מהו שימיר בו דהוי ליה שני גופין וקדושה אחת ומספקא ליה כדפרישית בלישנא דלעיל או שלא הומם אלא (אם) נתכפר באחר וניתק זה לעולה כשנמצא והוה ליה שתי קדושות וגוף אחד מהו שימיר ופירושא כדפרישית:
notes.en: Two bodies and two sanctities, what is the halakha? For example, where this second one was lost, he achieved atonement with another, and the second one was consigned to a burnt offering when it was found. What is the halakha? Since it is now a second [body] and another sanctity, he can substitute; or perhaps, in the end it comes by force of the first, and he cannot substitute. In another version, [that of] the Yerushalmi, we read it as two dilemmas: he designated a guilt offering and substituted for it, and it became blemished and he desacralized it onto another; what is the halakha as to whether he can substitute for it? For this is two bodies and one sanctity, and he is uncertain as I explained in the version above. Or where it did not become blemished, but he achieved atonement with another and this one was consigned to a burnt offering when it was found, so that it is two sanctities and one body; what is the halakha as to whether he can substitute? And the explanation is as I explained.

notes.he: דקא מערב להו בחדא היינו טעמא משום דחדא מגו חדא קא מיבעיא ליה. בדין אם תימצא לומר (הכי) קאמר אם תמצא לומר ב' גופין בקדושה אחת אין חוזר ומימר משום דבההיא קדושה הא כבר המיר בה חדא זימנא והם הכי נמי ב' קדושות וגוף אחד אין חוזרין וממירין דהא כבר המיר באותו גוף ב' גופין וב' קדושות מהו דבעיא עם המום ונתכפר מסתברא בב' גופין וב' קדושות כדאמרן לעיל:
notes.en: And Rabbi Avin, who combines them into one: this is the reason, because he asks one from within another. He is properly saying “if you say”: if you say that with two bodies in one sanctity one does not substitute again, because with that sanctity he already substituted once, and likewise with two sanctities and one body one does not substitute again, since he already substituted with that body, then what of two bodies and two sanctities? For the dilemma involves both the blemish and the atonement; it is reasonably two bodies and two sanctities, as we said above.

messages.text: The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

According to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that Rabbi Shimon holds that one cannot effect substitution and then effect substitution again for the same animal, if one designated an animal as a guilt offering with which to achieve atonement and substituted for it, and the initial guilt offering became blemished and he desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another animal, what is the halakha as to whether he can then effect substitution for this last animal? On the one hand, it is a different animal; on the other hand, it possesses the same sanctity.
messages.lead: The Gemara presents an alternative version of the previous dilemma. Rabbi Avin raises a dilemma:

notes.dh: בעי רבי אבין לדברי האומר כו'
notes.he: ויש בספרים ב' לשונות ורש"י פירש לשון שני של ירושלמי וכללא דמילתא היכא דהומם וחיללו על אחר ונתכפר באשם אחר פירוש כגון שנאבד הראשון ואח"כ נמצא וניתק הוא לעולה זהו שני גופין ושתי קדושות הומם וחיללו על אחר ולא נתכפר באשם אחר זהו שני גופין וקדושה אחת לא הומם אלא נתכפר באשם אחר וניתק זה לעולה כגון שנאבד ואחר כך נמצא אחר שנתכפר באשם אחר זהו שתי קדושות וגוף אחד וללשון שני ונתכפר באשם אחר רוצה לומר א"נ נתכפר וב' בעיות הן וכן גבי מוסיף חומש יש שתי לשונות כי הכא:
notes.en: Rabbi Avin raises a dilemma according to the one who says etc.: In the books there are two versions, and Rashi explained the second version, [that of] the Yerushalmi. The rule of the matter: where it became blemished and he desacralized it onto another, and he achieved atonement with another guilt offering, meaning, for example, that the first [replacement] was lost and afterward found and consigned to a burnt offering, this is two bodies and two sanctities. Where it became blemished and he desacralized it onto another and he did not achieve atonement with another guilt offering, this is two bodies and one sanctity. Where it did not become blemished, but he achieved atonement with another guilt offering and this one was consigned to a burnt offering, for example, it was lost and found after he achieved atonement with another guilt offering, this is two sanctities and one body. And according to the second version, “and he achieved atonement with another guilt offering” means “or alternatively he achieved atonement,” and they are two dilemmas. And so too with regard to adding one-fifth there are two versions, as here.

notes.he: ובהאי לישנא לא מיירי כלל בב' גופין וב' קדושות אלא או ב' קדושות וגוף א' או ב' גופין בקדושה אחת דהאי נתכפר באשם הוי כגון ונתכפר באשם בעיא אחריתי היא בב' קדושות גוף א' אמר אביי הידין קא מיבעיא ליה כו':
notes.en: Another version: Rabbi Avin raises a dilemma etc. And in this version he does not deal at all with two bodies and two sanctities, but with either two sanctities and one body, or two bodies in one sanctity; for this “he achieved atonement with a guilt offering” is as if [it said] “or he achieved atonement with a guilt offering,” a separate dilemma about two sanctities in one body. Abaye said: Which is he asking etc.

messages.text: If the first animal was lost and the owner achieved atonement by bringing another as a guilt offering, and the first animal was found and was consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, what is the halakha as to whether he can then effect substitution for it? On the one hand, it is the same animal; on the other hand, it possesses a different type of sanctity.

Which of these two is the essential dilemma he is raising? If his dilemma concerns a case of another type of sanctity in the same body, he should not raise the dilemma in the case where the initial guilt offering became blemished and he desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another animal. And if his dilemma concerns a case of another body with the same sanctity, he should not raise the dilemma in the case where the owner achieved atonement by bringing another animal as a guilt offering.
messages.quote: what is the halakha as to whether he can then effect substitution for this last animal?

notes.he: אי זו מהן הויא עיקר שאלתו אי קדושה אחרת באותו הגוף כו' כדפרישית דהיינו גוף אחד ושתי קדושות לא ניבעי הומם וחיללו כו' ורבי אבין חדא מגו חדא קא מיבעיא ליה ואת"ל קאמר. והשתא להאי לישנא לא בעי מידי משני גופים ושתי קדושות אלא ה"ק אם תימצי לומר גוף אחד באותה קדושה כו' ולהאי לישנא חשיב שני גופין וקדושה אחת חדא טפי משתי קדושות וגוף אחד:
notes.en: Abaye said: Which is he asking about? Which of them is the essence of his question? If another sanctity in the same body etc., as I explained, that is, one body and two sanctities, let him not ask about its becoming blemished and his desacralizing it etc. And Rabbi Avin asks one from within another, and he is saying “if you say.” And now, according to this version, he is asking nothing about two bodies and two sanctities; rather this is what he says: If you say that one body [another body] with the same sanctity etc. And according to this version, he counts two bodies and one sanctity as one step beyond two sanctities and one body.

messages.text: Rabbi Avin raises one dilemma as a result of the anticipated solution to another dilemma, as follows: If the initial guilt offering became blemished and he desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another animal, what is the halakha as to whether he can then effect substitution for the second animal?

Do we say that it is with the first guilt offering that he cannot effect substitution again, but with another body, even though it is sanctified with the same type of sanctity, he can effect substitution again? Or perhaps we say that with regard to any animal with the same type of sanctity, he cannot effect substitution again?

And if you say that with regard to this other body, since it maintains the same type of sanctity as the original animal one cannot effect substitution again, but what then of a case where the first animal was lost and the owner achieved atonement by bringing another animal as a guilt offering, and this first animal was then found and was consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering? What is the halakha as to whether he can effect substitution again for the same animal, since now its sanctity has changed?

Do we say that when Rabbi Yoḥanan states that the owner cannot effect substitution and then effect substitution again, this statement applies to the same body with the same type of sanctity, but as for the same body with another type of sanctity, he can effect substitution again? Or perhaps we say that even concerning another type of sanctity, since it is the same body, he cannot effect substitution again with it.
The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

One who redeems an animal that was originally consecrated as an offering and developed a blemish must pay an amount equivalent to its value and add an additional one-fifth of its value. But one who redeems an animal that was consecrated second, i.e., in place of a desacralized blemished offering, and then developed a blemish itself, must pay an amount equivalent to its value but does not add an additional one-fifth of its value.
messages.lead: § The Gemara cites a similar discussion.

notes.he: והיינו הקדש שני כגון שהומם הראשון וחיללו על אחר והוי האי אחר הקדש שני ואם הומם וחיללו אינו מוסיף עליו חומש ותמורה נמי הויא הקדש שני:
notes.en: But a second consecration does not add one-fifth: and this is a second consecration: for example, where the first became blemished and he desacralized it onto another, this other one is a second consecration; and if it became blemished and he desacralized it, he does not add one-fifth to it. And a substitute too is a second consecration.

notes.dh: אמר ר' יהושע] אהקדש ראשון מוסיף חומש [ולא אהקדש שני מוסיף חומש]
notes.he: כלומר בעלים שפודין הקדשן מוסיפין חומש כדכתיב ואם המקדיש יגאל ויסף וגו' ולא אם חללו אותו הקדש בדבר אחר שאותו דבר אחר נתפס הוא בהקדש ואם רוצין לפדותו בעלים אותו דבר אחר אין מוסיפין עליו חומש כדקאמר המקדיש ולא המתפיס:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said: For a first consecration one adds one-fifth, [but for a second consecration one does not add one-fifth]. That is to say, owners who redeem their consecrated property add one-fifth, as it is written: “And if he that consecrated it will redeem [his house], then he shall add” etc.; but not if they desacralized that consecrated property onto another item, for that other item is taken into consecration, and if the owners wish to redeem that other item, they do not add one-fifth to it, as it says: “he that consecrated it,” and not one who applies [sanctity].

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi? The verse states: “And if he that consecrated it will redeem his house, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of your valuation unto it, and it shall be his,” from which Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi infers that the requirement to pay an additional one-fifth applies to one who consecrates an item directly, but not to the one who applies the sanctity of another item to it.
messages.quote: does not add an additional one-fifth

verse.he: וְאִם־הַמַּקְדִּישׁ יִגְאַל אֶת־בֵּיתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית כֶּסֶף־עֶרְכְּךָ עָלָיו וְהָיָה לוֹ׃
verse.en: and if the one who has consecrated the house wishes to redeem it, one-fifth must be added to the sum at which it was assessed, and then it shall be returned.

messages.text: If one designated an animal as a guilt offering by which to achieve atonement and it became blemished, and he added one-fifth to its value and desacralized it, and he then used the consecrated money to purchase another guilt offering, which was then lost, and the owner achieved atonement by bringing another, third, animal as a guilt offering, and the second animal was found and consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, and then it developed a blemish, what is the halakha as to whether the owner must add one-fifth to its value when he redeems it?
messages.lead: Rabbi Avin raises a dilemma concerning a similar matter:

notes.he: כדלעיל דהוו להו שני גופים ושתי קדושות מהו:
notes.en: He designated a guilt offering to atone with it etc.: as above, so that they are two bodies and two sanctities; what is the halakha?

notes.he: וכי היכי כדקא בעי לעיל לענין תמורה אי מימר וחוזר ומימר בגוף א' וב' קדושות או בב' גופין וקדושה א' הכי נמי בעי לענין חומש]:
notes.en: [Rabbi Avin raises a dilemma: He designated a guilt offering etc. Just as he asked above with regard to substitution, whether one substitutes and then substitutes again with one body and two sanctities, or with two bodies and one sanctity, so too he asks with regard to one-fifth.]

messages.text: What is the dilemma he is raising? If he is raising a dilemma with regard to two bodies, i.e., two different animals, the problem should stand even if both are of one type of sanctity. If so, let the dilemma be raised even in a case where he did not achieve atonement through another guilt offering, and the second animal was never consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering.
messages.quote: whether the owner must add one-fifth to its value when he redeems it?

notes.he: לרבי אבין דסלקא אדעתין דבעיא דר' אבין לאו שני גופין ושתי קדושות בעי אלא בתרי מילי פליג מילתיה דקמייתא הוו שני גופין וקדושה אחת ואידך נתכפר באשם אחר כלומר שלא הומם הראשון אלא שאבד ונתכפר באחר ונמצא זה וניתק לעולה דהוו להו שתי קדושות וגוף אחד מהו הלכך פריך אביי הי מינייהו עיקר בעיא דר' אבין ליבעי להדיא ולישמע אידך מינה:
notes.en: What is the dilemma he is raising: Rabbi Avin? For it entered our minds that Rabbi Avin’s dilemma is not about two bodies and two sanctities, but that he divided his statement into two matters: the first is two bodies and one sanctity, and the other is “he achieved atonement with another guilt offering,” that is, the first did not become blemished but was lost, and he achieved atonement with another, and this one was found and consigned to a burnt offering, so that it is two sanctities and one body; what is the halakha? Therefore Abaye objects: Which of them is the essence of Rabbi Avin’s dilemma? Let him ask it explicitly, and we will learn the other from it.

notes.dh: אי שני גופין וקדושה אחת קמיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא נתכפר
notes.he: באחר אלא הומם הראשון וחיללו והוסיף עליו חומש דחומש לא שייך בקדשי מזבח בלא מום דהא תם לא נפיק לחולין והומם האי שני מהו כלומר מי אמרינן כיון דקדושה אחת היא אינו מוסיף בה חומש אחרינא או דילמא כיון דב' גופין נינהו מוסיף בה חומש וכי אמר ר' יהושע הקדש שני אינו מוסיף ביה חומש כגון מתפיס בעל מום לבדק הבית וחיללו בבעל מום אחר דהאי לא מחדש בה מידי אבל הכא דמתפיס תם בבעל מום דהאי חזי למזבח הקדש שני קרינן ביה דההוא קמא לא חזי אלא לדמי והאי חזי למזבח וקדושה חדשה היא:
notes.en: If he is raising a dilemma about two bodies and one sanctity, let him raise it without atonement: with another; rather: the first became blemished and he desacralized it and added one-fifth to it (for one-fifth has no relevance to sacrifices of the altar without a blemish, since an unblemished animal does not go out to non-sacred status), and this second one became blemished; what is the halakha? That is to say, do we say that since it is one sanctity he does not add another one-fifth to it, or perhaps since they are two bodies he adds one-fifth to it? And when Rabbi Yehoshua said that a second consecration does not add one-fifth, that is, for example, where one applies [the sanctity of] a blemished animal consecrated for Temple maintenance and desacralized it onto another blemished animal, for this one introduces nothing new. But here, where he applies [the sanctity] onto an unblemished animal from a blemished one, and this one is fit for the altar, do we call it a second consecration? The first was fit only for its monetary value, while this one is fit for the altar, and it is a new sanctity.

notes.he: וליבעי הכי הפריש אשם להתכפר לו והומם וחיללו על חברו והוסיף עליו חומש וחזר והומם זה וחיללו על אחר אם מוסיף עליו חומש שוב אי לא [אי] ב' קדושות וגוף א' אם מוסיף חומש אהקדש שני:
notes.en: Let him ask it without atonement, and let him ask thus: he designated a guilt offering to atone with it, and it became blemished, and he desacralized it onto another and added one-fifth to it, and then this one became blemished and he desacralized it onto another: does he add one-fifth to it again or not? [And if] two sanctities and one body: whether he adds one-fifth for a second consecration.

messages.text: And if he is raising a dilemma with regard to two types of sanctity, it should apply even in the case of one body. If so, let the dilemma be raised even in a case where the original animal did not become blemished but was simply lost and found after the owner atoned by means of another offering and thereby consigned the original animal to be sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.dh: אי שתי קדושות וגוף אחד מיבעיא ליה תיבעי ליה בלא הומם
notes.he: קודם שאבד אלא אבד והפריש אחרת ונתכפר בו ונמצא הראשון וניתק לעולה מהו מי אמרינן הקדש שני הוא שהרי נתכפר באחר וזה טפל לו ואם הומם ובא לחללו לא יוסיף עליו חומש או דלמא כיון דשתי קדושות נינהו ה"ל הקדש ראשון לענין זה ומוסיף חומש:
notes.en: If he is raising a dilemma about two sanctities and one body, let him raise it without its becoming blemished: before it was lost; rather: it was lost, and he designated another and achieved atonement with it, and the first was found and consigned to a burnt offering; what is the halakha? Do we say it is a second consecration, since he achieved atonement with another and this one is secondary to it, so that if it becomes blemished and he comes to desacralize it he does not add one-fifth to it? Or perhaps, since they are two sanctities, it is a first consecration in this respect, and he adds one-fifth?

notes.he: תיבעי בלא הומם ותבעי הכי הפריש אשם להתכפר בו ונאבד ונתכפר באחר ונמצא ראשון (דהויא עולה) [וניתק לעולה] היינו הקדש שני וגוף אחר:
notes.en: Let him ask it without the blemish, and let him ask thus: he designated a guilt offering to atone with it, and it was lost, and he achieved atonement with another, and the first was found (which is a burnt offering) [and was consigned to a burnt offering]: this is a second sanctity and another body.

messages.text: Rabbi Avin raises one dilemma as a result of the anticipated solution to another dilemma, as follows: If you say that in a case of two bodies and one type of sanctity the owner does not add one-fifth, perhaps that is because one-fifth was already added once to redeem an animal with that type of sanctity. If so, what is the halakha in the case of two bodies and two types of sanctity? Perhaps, since the second animal possesses a different sanctity, it is considered to possess its own original sanctity, rather than derivative sanctity, and therefore one who redeems it adds one-fifth.

notes.he: כלומר סיפא דבעייא דרבי אבין ארישא דמילתא קאי ולאו מילתא אחריתי היא אלא שני גופין ושתי קדושות בעי:
notes.en: One from within another: that is to say, the latter part of Rabbi Avin’s dilemma rests on the first part of the matter and is not a separate matter; rather he is asking about two bodies and two sanctities.

notes.he: אם תמצא לומר היינו חדא מגו חדא:
notes.en: He is saying “if you say”: “if you say” is what “one from within another” means.

notes.he: מי אמרי' כיון דשני גופין ושתי קדושות נינהו לא מיקרי הקדש שני ומוסיף חומש דהא בהא קדושה והאי גופא לא אתוסף חומשו או דלמא סוף סוף מכח קמא אתא (מעיקרא) והקדש שני הוא לגבי חומש. לישנא אחרינא ירושלמי וכלישנא בתרא דלעיל דבעיא דרבי אבין גבי תמורה גרסי' לה נמי הכא ופירושי מפרש:
notes.en: What is the halakha: do we say that since they are two bodies and two sanctities, it is not called a second consecration and he adds one-fifth, since with this sanctity and this body its one-fifth has not been added? Or perhaps, in the end it comes by force of the first, and it is a second consecration with regard to one-fifth? Another version, [that of] the Yerushalmi, like the latter version above of Rabbi Avin’s dilemma concerning substitution: we read it here too, and its explanation follows accordingly.

messages.text: The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

If one designated an animal as a guilt offering with which to achieve atonement, and it became blemished and he desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another animal, and he added one-fifth of its value, and the second animal was lost and the owner achieved atonement by bringing another, third, animal as a guilt offering, and the second animal was found and was consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, and then it developed a blemish, what is the halakha as to whether the owner must add one-fifth to its value when he redeems it?
messages.lead: The Gemara presents an alternative version of the previous dilemma. Rabbi Avin raises a dilemma:

messages.text: Which of these two is the essential dilemma he is raising? If he raises a dilemma with regard to the case of another type of sanctity in the same body, he should not raise the dilemma about a case where the initial guilt offering became blemished and he transferred its sanctity to another animal. And if his essential dilemma concerns the case of another body with the same type of sanctity, he could pose his dilemma with regard to a case where the second animal was not lost and found and consigned to be a burnt offering.
messages.quote: whether the owner must add one-fifth to its value when he redeems it?

messages.text: Rabbi Avin raises one dilemma as a result of the anticipated solution to another dilemma. If the initial guilt offering became blemished and he desacralized it by transferring its sanctity onto another, second, animal, what is the halakha as to whether the owner must add one-fifth to its value when he redeems it?

notes.he: ור' אבין חדא מגו חדא [קא מיבעיא ליה בדין אם תמצא לומר כו'] ולהאי לישנא אחרינא דר' אבין נמי לא קא מיירי כלל בב' גופין וב' קדושות כו'. וכהאי ל"א דלעיל:
notes.en: And Rabbi Avin asks one from within another, [he is properly saying “if you say” etc.]. And according to this other version of Rabbi Avin too, he does not deal at all with two bodies and two sanctities etc., like the other version above.

messages.text: Do we say that with regard to a second redemption of the first guilt offering he does not add one-fifth, since it is the same body and the same sanctity, but here, when it is another body, even though it maintains the same type of sanctity as the initial animal, he adds one-fifth, as it is considered to be directly consecrated?

The printed Aramaic of this question reads, with a bracketed correction: “Is it with the first guilt offering that he adds one-fifth, but with another body, even though it stands in the same sanctity, he [does not] add one-fifth?” The translation above follows a different understanding of the line.
Continued on 10a: “Or perhaps any animal with the same sanctity adds no fifth?” and then the case of the same body in another sanctity. That dilemma too shall stand unresolved.
